known_facts_book1: The fairyland ruled by Princess Ozma, made up of four countries — the Munchkins, Gillikins, Quadlings and Winkies — cornered around the Emerald City.
The travelers reach it only at the end, brought there by the Magic Belt rather than by the underground journey itself.
Dorothy has visited before; the Wizard once built it and ruled it.
A place where animals such as Jim and Eureka can talk and where the Sawhorse lives.

known_relations_book1.the Wizard: The man who built the Emerald City and once ruled the land.

not_in_this_book: the Land of Oz is reached through the underground tunnel
the Land of Oz turns out to be a dream

hallucination_signals: the tunnel leads straight to Oz

known_facts_book1: The green capital of the Land of Oz, built by the Wizard, where Ozma reigns.
Site of the reunion, the grand procession and the games, and of Eureka's trial in the Throne Room.
The travelers are wished into its streets by the Magic Belt.

known_relations_book1.Land of Oz: The fairyland it is capital of.

not_in_this_book: the Emerald City is captured by the Nome King

hallucination_signals: the Emerald City is only green through spectacles

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's home, where Uncle Henry and Aunt Em live on a farm.
Where Toto stayed behind while Dorothy travelled.
Where Ozma's Magic Belt sends Dorothy at the end of the book.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Her home, to which she returns.
known_relations_book1.Toto: Left behind there during the adventure.

known_facts_book1: The surface city where the Wizard was born and where his father named him.
The Wizard returned there after leaving Oz, only to find his old friends dead or moved away.

not_in_this_book: Omaha is in the Land of Oz

known_facts_book1: Uncle Bill Hugson's ranch in California, where Zeb works and where Dorothy and Uncle Henry were visiting.
Dorothy arrives nearby at Hugson's Siding, the train stop, at dawn.
Zeb and Jim are set down here by the Magic Belt in the closing scene.

not_in_this_book: Hugson's Ranch is in the Land of Oz

known_facts_book1: A beautiful underground valley reached through the glass mountain, lit by no sun or moon from an unseen source.
Its people are invisible from eating the dama-fruit, and so are the fierce bears that hunt them.
The travelers refuse the dama-fruit to stay visible; the nine piglets eat it and turn invisible.
The travelers cross it walking on the water to escape the invisible bears and reach Pyramid Mountain.

known_relations_book1.Champion: Overman-Anu, its greatest Champion, spoken of by the invisible people.
known_relations_book1.Pyramid Mountain: The mountain the travelers cross the valley to reach.

not_in_this_book: the Valley of Voe is in the Land of Oz
the people of Voe are visible

hallucination_signals: the Valley of Voe in Oz

known_facts_book1: A cone-shaped mountain on the far side of the Valley of Voe, its point lost in the clouds.
A spiral stairway cut inside it leads up to the Land of the Gargoyles.
Home, halfway up, to the Braided Man's factory of rustles and flutters; Cloud Fairies drift near its heights.

known_relations_book1.Gargoyles: The wooden people whose land lies at its top.

not_in_this_book: Pyramid Mountain is in the Land of Oz

known_facts_book1: A dark cave in the green glass mountain of the Mangaboo country, into which the animals are driven and walled up.
A tunnel leading up out of it carries the travelers on toward the Valley of Voe.

known_relations_book1.Mangaboos: The vegetable people who drive the animals into it.
known_relations_book1.Eureka: The kitten who escapes it to fetch help.

not_in_this_book: the Black Pit is in the Land of Oz
